newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram says wants land laws changed.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram says wants land laws changed.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Tuesday that he favoured changing land laws to promote private investment in roads.
"I hope we will review land laws, particularly ceiling laws, and find a way to promote (private) investment in the road sector," he told the World Economic Forum.
Currently, Indian laws restrict foreign ownership of land and in some cases cap how much a single person or company can own.
Chidambaram said some proposed private investments in the road sector were at an advanced stage.
But he said laws relating to land acquisition constituted the biggest stumbling block in attracting foreign investment into the road sector.
"If we can get over the problem of land acquisition, there is great scope for attracting foreign investment in the road sector," he said.
But he said urban land ceilings were "a very sensitive subject" with political overtones, and any change would require a cabinet decision.
He said, however, that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had hinted that he too favoured changing the land laws.
